messages.subject: X chromosome LOD threshold=0
parts:
Dear Dr. Broman

I contacted you before with some questions about the use of sex as covariate and the definition of a sex linkage group (post: Q re covariates and sex chromosome). Although I'm not defining a sex linkage group anymore, because it still recombine quite a lot, I still have some questions concerning my previous attempts.

My study systems consist on a CP cross, with the presence of sex chromosomes and sexual dimorphism. I have 314 individuals and 655 SNP markers distributed in 12 linkage groups.
Because I have sexual dimorphism in many of the traits I include sex as a covariate.
When I define the X chromosome and run the permutation test with method "em", perm.Xsp=TRUE and addcovar=sex, for many of the traits the X LOD threshold drops to 0.

I'm not really sure why this happens and what should be done with this result. Could you give some explanation?
I understand that defining the X chromosome include sex as an internal covariate, but I think one can still allowed for phenotypic differences between sexes by adding sex as covariate.

Thanks a lot!

Fernanda

I have no idea why that is happening. I don't think it should be happening.

karl
